subject: Psychiatry
subtopic: Intellectual disability and specific learning disorder
vignette: A 10-year-old boy has global developmental delays. He has difficulty with reasoning, memory, and abstract thinking, and his language skills are markedly below those of his peers. He struggles with academic work, communication, and daily living tasks and requires significant support for independence. Intelligence testing shows generalized cognitive impairment across multiple domains.
question: Which of the following best distinguishes intellectual disability from specific learning disorder in this patient?

options.text: Global cognitive deficits with impaired adaptive functioning across multiple domains
Normal intelligence with an isolated deficit in one academic subject for 6 months
Sudden recurrent motor and vocal tics present for over a year
Overwhelming fear of separation from home lasting more than 4 weeks
Refraining from speech in certain situations despite speaking in others

explanation_correct: Intellectual disability involves global cognitive deficits affecting reasoning, memory, abstract thinking, judgment, language, and learning, with impaired adaptive functioning that causes major difficulties in education, employment, communication, socialization, and independence. This contrasts with specific learning disorder, in which a specific academic skill is impaired but general intelligence and functioning are normal. Treatment includes psychotherapy, occupational therapy, and special education.

explanation_incorrect.B: Normal intelligence with an isolated academic deficit persisting at least 6 months describes specific learning disorder, not intellectual disability.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sudden recurrent motor and vocal tics lasting over a year describe Tourette syndrome, which is not a cognitive or adaptive functioning disorder.
explanation_incorrect.D: Overwhelming fear of separation lasting at least 4 weeks describes separation anxiety disorder, not a global cognitive deficit.
explanation_incorrect.E: Refraining from speech in certain situations despite speaking elsewhere describes selective mutism, not intellectual disability.

educationalObjective: Intellectual disability is global cognitive impairment with impaired adaptive functioning, distinguishing it from specific learning disorder with otherwise normal intelligence.

subject: Psychiatry
subtopic: Intellectual disability and specific learning disorder
vignette: An 11-year-old girl has persistent difficulty with reading despite average intelligence and adequate educational opportunity. After 9 months of focused reading intervention she still performs well below age-expected proficiency in that subject alone. Her math and writing skills are age appropriate, and she has no problems with socialization or activities of daily living.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis and management for this girl?

options.text: Intellectual disability; special education and occupational therapy
Autism spectrum disorder; behavioral and speech therapy
Specific learning disorder; academic support and counseling
Separation anxiety disorder; CBT and family therapy

explanation_correct: Specific learning disorder begins during the school-age years and involves inability to acquire or use information from a specific subject — here, reading — near age-expected proficiency for at least 6 months despite focused intervention. General functioning and intelligence are normal, which excludes intellectual disability. Management includes academic support, counseling, and extracurricular activities.

explanation_incorrect.A: Intellectual disability requires global cognitive deficits and impaired adaptive functioning; this girl's intelligence and other academic skills are normal.
explanation_incorrect.B: ADHD involves hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention across settings, not an isolated reading deficit with normal attention.
explanation_incorrect.C: Autism spectrum disorder requires social/communication deficits and restricted behaviors, which are absent in this girl with normal socialization.
explanation_incorrect.E: Separation anxiety disorder involves overwhelming fear of separation, not a specific academic skill deficit.

educationalObjective: Specific learning disorder is a single-subject skill deficit lasting at least 6 months despite intervention with normal general intelligence, managed with academic support.

subject: Psychiatry
subtopic: Intellectual disability and specific learning disorder
vignette: A 9-year-old boy has difficulty solving math problems at grade level despite extra tutoring for 8 months. Reading and writing are age appropriate, his intelligence is in the average range, and he functions well socially and independently. His parents ask why he struggles only in mathematics.
question: Which of the following statements about this boy's condition is most accurate?

options.text: His difficulties reflect global cognitive deficits affecting all subjects
He most likely has ADHD with inattention as the primary problem
General intelligence and overall functioning are normal, with impairment limited to a specific subject
He meets criteria for intellectual disability based on academic underachievement
His presentation is best explained by selective mutism

explanation_correct: This boy has specific learning disorder: impairment in a specific academic subject (math) near age-expected proficiency for at least 6 months despite focused intervention, with normal general intelligence, overall functioning, and adaptive skills. This is the key distinction from intellectual disability, which involves global cognitive deficits and impaired adaptive functioning. Treatment includes academic support and counseling.

explanation_incorrect.A: Global cognitive deficits affecting all subjects would indicate intellectual disability; his reading, writing, intelligence, and adaptive functioning are normal.
explanation_incorrect.B: ADHD requires hyperactivity/impulsivity/inattention in multiple settings, not an isolated math difficulty with otherwise normal functioning.
explanation_incorrect.D: Academic underachievement in one subject with normal intelligence does not meet criteria for intellectual disability.
explanation_incorrect.E: Selective mutism is an anxiety disorder involving refraining from speech in certain situations, unrelated to academic skill deficits.

educationalObjective: In specific learning disorder, intelligence and overall functioning are normal while a single academic subject is impaired for at least 6 months despite intervention.
